candidateEvidence.excerpt: Nature reports that five drug companies used 20,167 private protein structures to fine-tune a research AI model based on OpenFold3. On a held-out test, the reported model predicted more protein–molecule structures accurately than comparable models trained on public data alone. This is a research-model comparison, not an announcement of a new drug.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: The reported consortium fine-tuned OpenFold3 on 20,167 proprietary protein-ligand structures from five companies. Nature reports a 1,056-structure held-out evaluation, says the model is not public, and says the described study has not been peer reviewed.
This is reporting on an unavailable, unreviewed research model. It establishes neither a new drug nor patient benefit.

A protein model is an AI system that predicts how proteins and other molecules might fit together. A held-out test uses examples kept separate from training. The report says the extra data helped on that test, but the model is not public and the described study has not been peer reviewed.

A model benchmark asks whether a system makes better predictions. A clinical trial asks whether a treatment helps people. This report is the first kind. Ask whether a later headline reports a model, a tested drug, or a patient outcome.
